records.name: CHURCH OF ST MARY AND ALL SAINTS
records.officialName: Church of St Mary and All Saints
records.details:
HOLCOT MAIN STREET SP76NE (West side) 12/52 Church of St. Mary and All 02/11/54 Saints

- I

Church. C13, C14 with C19 restoration. Squared coursed lias with ashlar dressings. Lead and slate roofs. Aisled nave, chancel and west tower. Chancel, south elevation of 2-window range of 3-light square-headed windows. East window, 3-lights C19 with rounded tracery. North elevation of chancel has C19 vestry and organ chamber. Gabled roof with ashlar parapets. South aisle of 2-window range with porch between. Window to left of porch is C19. 2-light square-headed window, window to right is C14 three-light square-headed. Similar east window. Lean-to roof has castellated ashlar parapets. Gabled porch has triple chamfered arch and double stepped south door arch. Ashlar parapets and finial. Roof beam of porch is dated RH/l671/1.K. I.B. North aisle of 2-window range of one 3-light window with reticulated tracery and one 2-light with Y-tracery. Blocked door with double chamfered arch between windows. 2-light west window with Y-tracery. South nave clerestory of 4-window range of 2-light square headed windows. Shallow pitched roof with castellated ashlar parapets. North nave clerestory similar. West tower of 3 stages with flat buttresses to first and second stage. 2-light window in first stage and 2-light decorated bell chamber openings with transoms to each face of third stage. Castellated ashlar parapets with gargoyles at corners. Interior: Chancel has C19 double chamfered arch to vestry and organ chamber. Nave of 3-bays has decorated arcade of double chamfered arches with short piers of clustered shafts. Similar double chamfered chancel arch. Tall double chamfered tower arch. 3-light window opening at end of north aisle has reticulated tracery and is open to the vestry beyond. Chancel roof is C19, plain plastered panels. Nave roof is shallow C19. Stained glass to all chancel windows, all south aisle windows and bellfry window. Wall paintings, probably C14: at the west end of the south aisle probably representing the Ascension, Pentecost, Coronation of the Virgin and the Incredulity of St. Thomas. Near the south door, the resurrection. In the north aisle St. Thomas Becket and St. Catherine before the Emperor. Saints in window splays of north aisle with scroll decoration to the arches. All are very faded, the reputed descent of the Holy Ghost has disappeared. Monuments: Left of altar, Rev. Edward Halles died 1715 and family. Marble tablet with broken scroll pediment over. Right of altar similar plain tablet to other members of Halles family probably errected after 1724. Frances Maria Montgomery died 1794 plain oval tablet to right of altar. 4 mid C19 oval tablets to left of altar commemorate Montgomery family. Plain tablet to B. Drage 1797 south aisle. Hatchment AR/1711. Font dated 1889 may incorporate medieval bowl. (Buildings of England: Northamptonshire, p.260).

Listing NGR: SP7923169830

records.name: HOLCOT WAR MEMORIAL
records.details:
SP76NE

12/50

HOLCOT 

BACK LANE

Holcot War Memorial

(Formerly listed as War Memorial)

II

The war memorial stands on a road junction near the centre of the village, where Back Lane branches off Moulton Road. It comprises a c. 4 m tall, medieval-style, Weldon stone cross with an elaborate foliate head. That stands on a squat two-stage octagonal shaft which rises from a square plinth on a stepped octagonal base of Derbyshire stone. Around this is a modern pebble surround with kerb (not included in listing). Slate panels are inset in the plinth. That to the front is inscribed THIS CROSS WAS GIVEN BY/ MRS E.L. DANIELS/ THE PATRON OF THIS LIVING. The rear face is inscribed TO THE GLORY OF GOD/ AND IN MEMORY OF THE MEN/ FROM THIS PARISH/ WHO FELL IN THE GREAT WAR/ 1914 – 1919/. GREATER LOVE/ HATH NO MAN THAN THIS. The names of those who died in the war appear on the other two faces. The name of a villager who died in the Second World War was added on the front panel.

Sources; Northampton Mercury 20 February and 30 July 1920

Listing NGR: SP7924269681

records.name: POLLYS COTTAGE
records.details:
HOLCOT BACK LANE SP76NE (North side) 12/49 Polly's Cottage

- II

House. Mid C18. Regular coursed lias with slate roof. Originally 2-unit plan. 2 storeys with attic, 2-window range of casements under wood lintels. Central entrance now blocked. Ashlar gable parapets, brick stacks at end. C19 extension to left. Extension to right not of special architectural interest. Blank tablet to left gable. Interior: Open fireplace with chamfered bressumer over; chamfered ceiling beams.

Listing NGR: SP7937669674

records.name: THE OLD RECTORY
records.details:
HOLCOT BRIXWORTH ROAD SP76NE 12/51 The Old Rectory 22/12/71 (Formerly listed as The Rectory)

- II

Rectory, now house. Late C18. Squared coursed lias with C20 concrete tile roof. Double depth plan. 2 storeys with attic. 3-window range of sashes with glazing bars to first floor and C20 French doors to ground floor all under flat arch heads. Central 4-panelled double doors with wooden pillars flanking and plain entablature over. Ashlar gabled parapets and brick and rendered stacks at ends. Rear and right sides rendered. Right gables have 2 attic casements with leaded lights, half gable has sashes with glazing bars. Interior:late C18 staircase with quarter turn.

Listing NGR: SP7919169812

records.name: HOLLY BUSH FARMHOUSE
records.details:
HOLCOT POPLAR LANE SP76NE (West side) 12/55 Holly Bush Farmhouse

- II

Farmhouse. Probably late C17. Coursed rubble lias with thatch roof. L-shaped plan. 2 storeys with attic. Main front elevation of 2-window range of 2-light casements with leaded lights at first floor and wood casements at ground floor all under wood lintels, C19 half glazed door to right with blocked window above. Elavation to right similar. Gabled roof with ashlar gable parapets and kneelers, brick and stone stacks at ends. Roof dormer to north. C18 outbuildings attached to south. Interior: East room has open fireplace with chamfered bressumer, kitchen has chamfered beams and wall cupboard with panelled doors probabaly late C17. Dogleg stair, some plant: doors with strap hinges. Butt purlin roof structure.

Listing NGR: SP7935269786

records.name: IVY HOUSE
records.details:
HOLCOT SYWELL ROAD SP76NE (North side) 12/57 Ivy House

- II

House. Early C18. Coursed lias rubble with thatched roof. L-shaped plan, originally of 3 units with through passage. 2-storey, 2-window range of casements with leaded lights to first floor and wood casements to ground floor, all under wood lintels. Central C19 half glazed door under wood lintel. Gabled roof with eyebrow dormers, ashlar gable parapets and kneelers and brick stacks at ridge and end. Rear, similar, has casements with leaded lights. Range of C18 barns with C19 roofs attached to rear. Interior: Chamfered ceiling beams to ground-floor rooms.

Listing NGR: SP7930769727

records.name: POPLAR FARM
records.details:
HOLCOT POPLAR LANE SP76NE (East side) 12/54 Poplar Farm

- II

Farmhouse. Early C19. Squared coursed lias with slate roof. Symmetrical 2-unit plan. 2 storeys, 2-window range of sashes with glazing bars under flat arch heads. Central 4-panelled door. Early C18 buildings with C19 alterations attached to left. Lunette to ground floor at rear. Interior not inspected but noted as having early C19 staircase.

Listing NGR: SP7940169773

records.name: MANOR HOUSE
records.details:
HOLCOT RECTORY LANE SP76NE (North side) 12/56 Manor House

- II

Manor House. Datestone 1664. Squared coursed lias with C20 concrete tile roof. Originally probably L-shaped plan. 2 storeys. Main front of 2-window range of dormers with 3-light stone mullions set in dormers with ashlar parapets, C20 casements at ground floor. Cross wing to right has similar 2-light stone mullion set in dormer. Gabled roof with ashlar gable parapets. Brick and stone stacks at ridge and end. Datestone in left dormer. Elevation to right: similar 2-window range of 3-light stone mullioned windows. C19 wing added to garden front in similar style has main entrance with 4-centred head and C19 ribbed door, in elevation to left.Interior: All rooms in C17 wing have chamfered ceiling beans, kitchen in cross wing has remains of open fireplace with bressumer. C19 staircase in hall has decorative newels. C19 fireplaces to first floor rooms and ground floor room right of hall.

Listing NGR: SP7913269916

records.name: BROOK COTTAGE WALL DENE
records.details:
HOLCOT SYWELL ROAD SP76NE (South side) 12/58 Brook Cottage and Wall Dene

- II

Two houses, probably originally 3 with workshops. Datestone 1725. Squared coursed lias with thatch roof. 4-unit plan with cross gabled wing to left. Single storey with attic, 5-window range of casements with glazing bars and wood lintels. Blocked entrance to left. Cross wing has ashlar gable parapets and kneelers. Brick stacks at ridge. Datestone to right of cross wing. East elevation of Wall Dene similar with 3-window range of eyebrow dormers. C19 doors to rear and side. Interior has chamfered ceiling beams to ground floor rooms.

Listing NGR: SP7944169700
